hook.text: Design a URL shortener. Prompts like this one are where interviews have grown: fewer take-home projects, and more live design discussion, where every choice gets asked why.

plan.text: Five questions, and one design carried through all of them: how to start, what to estimate, the first diagram, what can take it down, and what goes in front of it.

q1.text: Question one. How do you approach an open-ended system design question? Not by drawing boxes. First, clarify the requirements, in two lists.

q1-func.text: Functional: what the system must do. Shorten a long URL, and send anyone who opens the short one to the long one. Then ask about the edges: custom aliases? Links that expire?

q1-nonfunc.text: Non-functional: scale, latency, availability and consistency. Redirects must be fast and almost never fail, and a short link must never start pointing somewhere else.

q1-steps.text: Then estimate the load, define the API, sketch a high-level design, and only then drill into the bottlenecks.

q1-why.text: The second list is the one that shapes the design: the same two features, at a thousand users or at a billion redirects a day, are different systems. Say each assumption out loud, so the interviewer can correct it before you build on it.
